topics.title: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment

concepts.learning_objective: Define bisection and the perpendicular bisector, and justify the eye construction using congruent triangles.
Use the fact that every point equidistant from X and Y lies on the perpendicular bisector of XY.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a segment with an unmarked ruler and a compass and explain which conditions are necessary.

topics.title: A 90 degree angle at a point and rope methods of the Sulba-Sutras
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Construction of a 90 degree Angle at a Given Point; Construction Methods in Sulba-Sutras)

concepts.learning_objective: Construct a 90 degree angle at a point on a line, or a perpendicular from a point outside it, using the perpendicular bisector method.
Describe the Sulba-Sutra rope construction of a perpendicular bisector and justify why it works.
Bisect any angle with a ruler and compass and justify the method by the SSS congruence condition.
Obtain angles such as 45, 22.5 and 75 degrees by combining constructed angles with bisection.

topics.title: Copying an angle and drawing parallel lines
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Repeating Units and Repeating Angles; Construction of a Line Parallel to the Given Line)

concepts.learning_objective: Make an exact copy of a given angle with a ruler and compass and justify it by SSS congruence.
Construct a line parallel to a given line through a point by copying a corresponding angle.

topics.title: Arch designs
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Arch Designs: Trefoil Arch; A Pointed Arch)

concepts.learning_objective: Construct symmetric support lines for trefoil and pointed arches using equal angles and equal lengths.
Identify the line of symmetry of an arch design and predict the effect of unequal support lines.

topics.title: Regular hexagons, the 60 degree angle and related constructions
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Regular Hexagons; Construction of a 60 degree angle; Related Constructions)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why six congruent equilateral triangles fit around a point to form a regular hexagon.
Construct a 60 degree angle through an equilateral triangle and use it to obtain 120, 30 and 15 degree angles.
Reason with angles to show that the points of a six-pointed star built on a regular hexagon are equilateral triangles.

topics.title: Tangrams and tiling a region with 2 x 1 tiles

concepts.learning_objective: State what tiling is and recall the tangram as a set of seven pieces cut from a square.
Decide whether an m x n grid can be tiled with 2 x 1 tiles by counting unit squares.

topics.title: The black-and-white colouring argument and tiling the plane

concepts.learning_objective: Use black-and-white colouring to prove that a region cannot be tiled with 2 x 1 tiles.
Identify regular polygons that tile the plane and explain this using the angles that meet at a point.
